label: perf-types-5y
_why: TICK-COST ISOLATION, PART 4 — IS THE JOURNAL-ENTRY COST PER ENTRY TYPE, AND IS THE base_values ROUTE THE PRICE OF THE DAM CAPS? (the user's standing go-ahead of 2026-10-08, the window to 07:15). Batch 3 (20261009_020736) run 3 read x10 research entries that can NEVER show (is_shown_when_inactive/possible always no) at ~0.9 s/yr per 204-entry copy — two thirds of a working copy's 1.4 — with the monthly tick 189 -> 578 ms: the engine pays per entry TYPE per country whatever its conditions. Arms (the jex book, config/mod_config.perf-*.json): daj10 = 1,440 dam survey journal-entry types (copies never added by anything: existence only) — is the per-type price general? (n=2); r1s = the research entries with ONE stage (inception) instead of three — 68 entry types instead of 204, the type count a merged-stage design would have; a probe, not a book (one grant per technology instead of three) (n=3); dcm = the 144 dam caps as ONE country static modifier added to every country at the start instead of 144 base_values lines (n=2) — if dcm = full the cost is the caps on every country whatever the route, and the fix is to give them only to the countries that need them (static_mode country_modifier_tech, which costs nothing before the dam technology); full (n=2) as the same-night reference. AMENDED before launch: das3 = the 144 cap lines x3 (432 lines) (n=2) — batch 3 read the original 144 lines as free at n=1 (ds = full) while x10 cost ~2.2 s/yr per copy: linear or superlinear? The vanilla run was dropped (batch 3 carries four).
